title: Simply supported beam-column with uniform load: second-order moment and deflection

source.work: Bentley Systems, STAAD.Pro Help, Verification Examples (public documentation, docs.bentley.com)
source.edition: STAAD.Pro Help v21 build (pages refer to the STAAD.Pro 2023 sample files), read 2026-11-22
source.notes: problem statement taken from the vendor page (text and input listing). The page cites: AISC, Specification for Structural Steel Buildings, 2005, p. 16.1-435, Case 1 (the 2005 edition was not opened; the same benchmark of the 2022 edition is in ../aisc-commentary) - NOT opened for this project; no number is taken from it. The page's 'theory' values are recorded as printed; the program's own results are not used.

analysis: Plane problem in the global X-Y plane (Y vertical); the out-of-plane DOFs (uz, rx, ry) of every node are held; in-plane bending about local z. Beam of 40 ft = 480 in, simply supported (the far end free to move axially), W10x60 with the moment of inertia the page gives, Iz = 341 in^4, E = 29,000 ksi (the page's closed form uses the full E); uniform load 0.1 kip/ft downward and axial compression 100 kip. Second-order analysis (exact stability functions). The area does not enter the targets (placeholder 10 in^2); Iy = 1000 Iz so that no out-of-plane buckling enters. Reference values: computed here from this statement (verification/derive/vendor_reference.py); the textbook cited by the vendor page was not opened and no number is taken from it.

quarantine.diagnosis: All targets are reproduced (the reference values of the ODE oracle to 1e-6, the page's printed values at their printed precision), and the engine agrees with the ODE oracle on this model (tier A). Tier C does not pass: engine and OpenSeesPy differ by 9.89e-4 in the rotation at the pinned end (allowed 9.88e-4). Tier C allows a difference of 1e-6 plus the ESTIMATED discretisation error of the foreign solver (OpenSeesPy with a linearised P-Delta transformation and a finite number of elements per member), which is an estimate and not a bound (docs/VERIFICATION.md, section 7); here the difference exceeds it by less than 1 %. The engine's result is the exact solution of the second-order member equations, so the disagreement lies in the foreign solver's discretisation; but under the rule that nothing is published when a tier disagrees, the problem is quarantined.
